about.title: Escalon Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Escalon is a small, tight-knit farming town, but its roads still carry a steady flow of local and pass-through traffic. Rt 120, Mchenry Avenue, Escalon Avenue, and Main Street see the bulk of reported collisions, and public data shows crashes cluster on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., likely tied to school, work, and farm-equipment traffic converging at once. When a collision causes injury, the first hours and days matter: insurance adjusters move fast, evidence disappears, and memories fade. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent you directly — we simply connect injured Escalon residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, deal with insurers, and help protect a claim from the start. The service is free to use, and any attorney you're matched with works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Whether the crash happened near town on Rt 120 or on a quieter residential street, getting informed early can make a real difference.

whyChoose.title: Why Escalon Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim, but if a government entity (like a county road agency) may be responsible, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early helps preserve your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for a crash on Escalon Avenue or Main Street, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure fault is assessed fairly rather than assumed against you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and any attorney you're matched with works on contingency — no fee unless there's a recovery. That means you can get informed advice without financial risk.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use those statements to shift blame or minimize what they owe. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on Rt 120 or another busy Escalon corridor?
items.answer: Corridors like Rt 120, Mchenry Avenue, and Escalon Avenue see a meaningful share of the town's reported injury collisions, especially on Thursday afternoons. Location alone doesn't determine fault or outcome, but it can affect what evidence is available, such as traffic camera footage or witness accounts. An attorney can help identify what's worth preserving quickly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Escalon?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If your claim might involve a government entity, such as a road maintained by the county, that deadline can be as short as six months. Because these timelines are strict, it helps to talk to an attorney sooner rather than later.
